**How the phase ends:** At the end of 1972 the war is on the verge of a settlement that both governments in Vietnam regard as provisional. The Easter Offensive has failed to destroy the ARVN or the Thieu government, at a cost to the PAVN of most of the armour it committed (by one count 134 T-54s, 56 PT-76s and 60 T-34s) and, on the historical count, about 100,000 men [H64]. The ARVN has held at An Loc and Kontum and retaken Quang Tri City, but has lost Quang Tri north of the Thach Han, the western Highlands and the border areas of III Corps, and its losses are given variously from about 10,000 killed to about 39,000 dead in the period [H64]. Almost a million South Vietnamese have been made refugees, about 600,000 of them in government camps [H64].

In this war the PAVN's losses for the year are higher than that count, and higher in particular formations. The GBU-38 cells added perhaps a fifth to the losses of the B-2 Front's divisions around An Loc, the siege box destroyed about a third of the guns brought to Kontum before the assault and broke the 320th Division's assault short of the wire, and the radar-bombing of the armour on the DMZ destroyed some 20–30 vehicles before they reached the firebases (EV000-74, EV000-76, EV000-77) [X-005]. Taken together I put the PAVN's killed and wounded in 1972 at about 7,000–10,000 above the historical figure, roughly a tenth more, concentrated in the 5th, 7th and 9th Divisions and the 320th and 2nd Divisions, which are the formations that will fight Phuoc Long, Ban Me Thuot and Xuan Loc [X-MT01]. The North replaces that difference within its flow of men for 1973 [E: one to two months of a replacement flow to the South of the order of 100,000 men a year or more in 1973–74]. What it does not replace as quickly is the experienced cadre killed in the measured assaults, and the 7th and 9th Divisions enter 1974 with greener companies than history's [X-MT01].

The countryside ends 1972 in two parts. Where a PAVN division came into the peopled lowlands, in northern Binh Dinh and Quang Tri, the gains of 1964–71 were lost and the hamlets returned to the state history left them in (EVMT01-1). In the held belt of the Delta and around Saigon the posts held through the year, the Front's infrastructure inside the post line did not return, and the files that will open the "war of the flags" survived intact (EVMT01-2). In Saigon the decree powers and the end of the hamlet elections took back the government's claim to the hamlets' consent, as they did historically (EVMT01-3). The historical land programme has by now distributed about a million hectares of its own, and the margin of the 1964 titling over history has narrowed to its six years of head start and the councils that confirmed it [H] [X-MT01]. Night control and the Front's weakness in the held belt remain one band better than history's; the government's legitimacy has returned to history's; and the Special Branch's knowledge of the infrastructure, which the historical police and Phoenix had largely caught up with by 1972, is one band better rather than two [X-MT01].

The lesson both sides draw is the same. The ARVN held where American air power was decisive, at An Loc and Kontum, and where American advisers coordinated it; it broke where its leadership failed, at Quang Tri and Tan Canh. The settlement about to be signed removes the American advisers and the American air power and leaves the PAVN in the South, while the North's air defences and economy recover. Hanoi needs only to rebuild, wait for the Americans to be gone, and choose its time.

The aircraft are still flying at the end of 1972, still American, and under the agreement about to be signed they will soon have no American strike force to cue. The Republic keeps nothing of them: no aircraft, no exploitation cells, no practice in using either.

The ARVN has held An Loc and Kontum more cheaply than history's, and has learned more completely that it holds besieged towns with American bombers measured onto the enemy by American analysts (EV000-76, EV000-77). The agreement about to be signed takes both away. The Republic enters 1973 more confident than history's and more dependent [X-005].

The ARVN's regiments and battalions have fought the offensive better than history's, and its divisions and corps no better: Quang Tri was lost by orders, and the column on Highway 1 was saved in part by a regiment (EV000-78). It has learned, from An Loc and Kontum, to use American air with an educated staff's precision, and it has no air of its own that its plans can rest on (F007-23) [X-007].

### Phase VI — Paris, the endgame, and 1975 (Jan 1973 – Dec 1975)

*End of phase against the historical state: POP.night_control 35–55 (history 0; low) · POP.night_control.II_corps 10–25 (history 0; low) · POP.night_control.III_corps 60–80 (history 0; low) · POP.night_control.IV_corps 65–85 (history 0; low) · POP.displacement +300 to +600 against history (low) · POP.gvn_legitimacy 0 to +5 against history (low) · GVN.political_stability 0 (history 2; low) · VCI.strength -40% to -15% against history (low) · ENEMY.engagement_control -5 to +2 against history (low) · TRAIL.tonnage_arriving -20% to +20% against history (low) · ARVN.effectiveness -35% to -15% against history (low) · ARVN.self_sufficiency +5 to +10 against history (low) · ARVN.self_sufficiency.logistics +3 to +8 against history (low) · ARVN.self_sufficiency.fire_support +3 to +8 against history (low) · US.casualties 0 (history 2; high) · US.political_tolerance 3 (history 2; low) · US.political_tolerance.public 0 to +2 against history (medium) · US.political_tolerance.congress 950–1,275 (history 700; medium) · US.political_tolerance.administration 4 (history 3; medium) · NEGOT.position 3 (history 1; low).*

Phase VI is the war without the Americans. The Paris Agreement of January 1973 takes US forces out and returns the prisoners; it leaves the PAVN in the South, the Thieu government in Saigon, and the war to be decided between them. The ceasefire never holds. In 1973 Saigon is on the offensive, recovering hamlets and roads, while the North rebuilds; in 1974 the two are evenly matched, and the ARVN, short of ammunition, fuel and spare parts as American aid falls, bleeds in a war of attrition it cannot sustain; in January 1975 the North tests whether the United States will respond to the seizure of a province, and when it does not, it commits its army to the Highlands [H72].

The shape of the phase is three slow years and a fast spring. The constraints that bind the American role are now law, not policy: the Case–Church amendment ends all US combat activity in Indochina from 15 August 1973, and Congress cuts military aid. In Hanoi, the 21st Plenum of October 1973 returns to revolutionary violence, and the PAVN builds a road network east of the mountains, a fuel pipeline into the South and an army of corps. In Saigon, the economy, hit by the oil shock and the departure of the Americans whose spending had sustained it, and a government that has narrowed its base, face the offensive of 1975 with an army spread thin across the whole country.

In this war the army that fights the last three years has been built for ten years around the belt-fed gun and the abundance of American ammunition, and the ration of 1974 finds it more dependent on volume than the historical one (EV000-89). It fights the attrition of 1974 with better weapons than its enemy and too few rounds to use them, and the hoards it builds against the ration are lost with Hue and the Highlands (EV000-91, EV000-94, EV000-95).

The bombers leave in August 1973 without bombing Neak Luong, and the coordinate cell is disbanded with nothing in the VNAF to send coordinates to (EV000-86). The ARVN fights 1974 and the defence of Phuoc Long with plans written for an air force that no longer comes, and loses Thuong Duc and Phuoc Long as history did, with its officers knowing exactly what they lack (EV000-91, EV000-92).

Phung Hoang outlives the Americans as a Vietnamese programme and helps the Republic's offensive of 1973 in the Delta; its national file, consolidated in Saigon since 1971, is still in the Central Intelligence Organization's building at the end of 1975, and the province files of Quang Ngai and Quang Tin are taken when those provinces fall in March (EV000-84, EV000-94, EV000-98). The advisers are gone in March 1973, and nothing of their eighteen months survives them but the counterparts who remember them.

The officer reforms leave the Republic in its last three years an officer corps that knows precisely what it lacks. Its battalion and regimental commanders, educated on a doctrine built around American fire, plan the battles of 1974 for a weight of fire the ration no longer allows (EV000-91). Its staff college writes, in November 1974, the only serious plan the Republic ever had for a defence on reduced resources; in March 1975 the President rejects it entirely and orders everything held, and its method is used a year late, for the evacuation of Da Nang in May (EV000-95, EV011-3).

In this war the last ration also fell on an army that made two-fifths of its own small-arms ammunition, a third of its 105mm rounds and nearly all of its radio batteries, from imported powder and semiconductors (EV000-89). The domestic plants stretched each ammunition and communications dollar, made the attrition of 1974 somewhat cheaper and changed no position the PAVN chose to take (EV000-91), gave Phuoc Long more rounds than it could fire (EV000-92), and in 1975 were still the Republic's (EV011-3).

In this war there is no Watergate, and the President who wrote Thieu his promises is in office to the end of the record. Case–Church passes as historically, so that the bombers he promised cannot lawfully return, but the War Powers Resolution fails in the House, the Republicans of 1974 do not desert him, the midterm costs his party about 22 House seats instead of 49, and the fiscal 1975 appropriation is about $950 million, which the Republic's own plants stretch to buy about what $1.2 billion bought historically (EV000-86, EV000-89, EV011-1) [X-011]. The Republic fights 1974 near the 1973 allowance. In March 1975, with a year's fuel and a President who has asked Congress for its bombers and been refused, Thieu refuses the Dalat staff college's withdrawal and orders the Highlands and I Corps held (F011-20); the Highlands are lost in five weeks instead of ten days and Hue in an ordered withdrawal in April, and on 31 March the Politburo, which historically resolved on 25 March to take Saigon before the rains, has no double collapse to resolve on and puts Saigon back to the dry season of 1975–76 (EV000-94, EV000-95, EVMT01-4) [X-011]. The Republic ends 1975 smaller, holding III and IV Corps and the coast from Nha Trang south, with its general reserve brought back from Da Nang by sea and its fall expected in the first months of 1976 (EV011-3) [X-011].

**How the phase ends:** In this war Phase VI does not end with the fall of Saigon. On 31 December 1975 the Republic of Vietnam holds III and IV Corps, the coast from Nha Trang south and about half the population of 1974; the PAVN holds the Highlands, I Corps and the central coast north of Khanh Hoa, and five corps are assembled for an offensive on the capital in the first months of 1976 (EV011-3) [X-011]. That is a conclusion and not an assumption. The date of 30 April 1975 was set in Hanoi by a resolution to finish before the rains, and the resolution was made possible by the double collapse of I and II Corps in the second half of March; in this war Thieu's decision of 11–14 March went the other way, the Highlands were lost in a five-week siege instead of a ten-day rout, Hue in an ordered withdrawal on 18 April instead of a collapse on 25 March, and the Politburo, without a collapse to resolve on, put Saigon back to the dry season (EV000-94, EV000-95, EVMT01-4) [X-011]. The mechanism was political and at the top: a President in Washington who did not fall, an appropriation near the 1974 level, and a President in Saigon who believed, on that evidence, that he need not give anything up (F011-20, F011-21). It bought a season, and it was bought at a price. The refusal of the Dalat study cost the Republic half its Highland force and the 2nd Division, which a planned withdrawal in the dry season would have saved, and its reserve spent the spring at Da Nang, five hundred kilometres from the capital, until SOUTHERN WALL brought it home in May.

The Republic that enters 1976 is not the historical Republic, and it is not a Republic that has survived. Its fall is expected in the dry season of 1976, by my estimate between February and May, from an offensive on the capital by five corps that it has a rebuilt reserve, a full arsenal, its Delta and its capital's belt to meet, and no American air power (EV011-3) [X-011]. Rung (b) by the test of rules/RUNGS.toml, because Saigon stands past 30 April 1975; the outcome in its own terms is a reprieve of about a year, and the record ends before it is spent. The Paris Agreement had removed the American forces and kept the PAVN in the South; Congress had written the end of American combat into law and would not unwrite it for a President who asked; American military aid had fallen less than history's but had fallen; and the government in Saigon, more stable than at any time since 1963, faced an enemy that had rebuilt after 1972 and chose its moment, and then chose to wait.

At the end of 1974, on the eve of Phuoc Long, the held belt of the Delta and the Saigon region was held at night more firmly than history's, and the Front's district committees there had lost about twice the historical share of their members in 1973 (EV000-84) [X-006]; the Special Branch's knowledge of the infrastructure was still the better for its ten years of files; the government's standing in the hamlets was history's, after the decrees of 1972; the army's battalions were better led and its divisions and corps no better; and the army as a whole was more dependent than history's on American fire it no longer had, and knew it (EV000-91, EV000-92) [X-MT01]. In this war the army had also fought 1974 near the 1973 allowance, with its aircraft flying and its relief columns fuelled, and lost perhaps 2,500–6,500 fewer men in the year than history's 30,000, a judgment on the two rates named in EV000-91 [X-008] [X-011]. At the end of 1975 the held belt and the files are still the Republic's, and the end vector measures a state that still exists.

Hanoi's posture never changed. It was committed to armed reunification throughout, from the Ninth Plenum of December 1963 to the resolution of October 1975 that set the offensive on Saigon for 1976, through the losses of 1965–68 and 1972 and the delay of 1975, and it accepted the Paris Agreement as a step towards that end. The timing of its campaign was its own, set by its army's road, the season and, in March 1975, by a map that did not offer it the collapse history had (EVMT01-4). The US war in Vietnam, from the advisory years to 1973, cost more than 58,000 American dead [H]. The Vietnamese dead, military and civilian, northern and southern, are counted in the millions by most estimates, and the record of them is less precise than the record of the Americans [H].

The squad guns and the marksmen's rifles of the ARVN's II Corps and of the 1st and 2nd Divisions are in the PAVN's hands by the end of the spring, with the hoards of Quang Ngai and the Highlands; the hoard at Hue was destroyed in place, and the hoards of III and IV Corps are still the Republic's [X-004] [X-011].

The Republic's defence of every besieged town had been built since 1971 around American bombers and American coordinates, and both were gone by the end of 1973 (EV000-86, EV000-92) [X-005]. At Pleiku in April 1975 it fought a siege without them, on fuel and rounds, and held three weeks (EV000-95).

The officers the reforms made fought 1975 as well as any part of the RVNAF fought it. Their best staff plan was refused in March and used in May, for SOUTHERN WALL and the rebuilding of the reserve (EV000-95, EV011-3). The board's files, with the evaluation report of every officer since 1964, are in the Joint General Staff's compound at the end of 1975 [X-007] [X-011].

The Republic's own plants stretched its aid dollar by about a third to two-fifths, kept its radios on the air through 1974, and in 1975 were the arsenal of an army that had lost its northern hoards; they shortened no collapse and lengthened none, because the spring of 1975 was decided by orders, families and an enemy who chose his ground, and at the end of the year they are still the Republic's (EV000-89, EVMT01-4, EV011-3) [X-008] [X-011].

# Card 014 — 1st Special Forces Operational Detachment-Delta (Delta Force) at full commitment, under a newly formed MACV joint special operations command from August 1964

*Memorandum 014 · status part2 · full record: memos/014/ · generated by fie.py*

## P014a · 1st Special Forces Operational Detachment-Delta (SFOD-D, Delta Force), US Army, in its 2026 configuration and at full strength: the whole unit committed to Vietnam, with its assault squadrons, its reconnaissance and surveillance squadron, its organic aviation squadron and its support squadrons, without the wider JSOC package (no 160th SOAR, no dedicated JSOC ISR wing); missions: hunting PAVN and VC leadership and the infrastructure, COSVN and the base areas, POW recovery, raids into the North and reconnaissance, across the borders only where and when history's forces went
the whole unit, full commitment [U]; ~1,000–1,500 personnel of whom ~250–350 operators [E: open-source estimates of Delta's strength, D1] · spaces ~1,000–1,500 [E: the whole unit; no ceiling (CONFIG troop_ceiling = NONE)] · arrives 1964-09-01 · FIND, FIX, STRIKE, SUBVERT · ground

**Key figures.**
- Unit: established 19 November 1977 [M014·S1]; 2026 strength about 1,000–1,500, of whom about 250–350 operators [E: S1's 2001 figures grown by D Squadron and the support squadron]
- Organisation: four assault squadrons (two assault troops and a reconnaissance troop each; assault troop four teams of 5–6), G Squadron (advanced force), E Squadron (company of light helicopters and King Airs), signal and support squadrons [M014·S1] [M014·S2]
- Arrival 1 September 1964; headquarters 15 August 1964 [E: two weeks after the Tonkin reports]
- Borders as history: Laos from 18 October 1965 within the ambassador's limits; Cambodia from September 1967, foot reconnaissance only; the North only at Son Tay, 21 November 1970 [M014·S3] [M014·S5] [U]
- Raids in the South at maturity: about 40–120 a month; 15–35% reach a listed cadre at district level or above; about 80–400 such cadre a year [E: D5]
- Reconnaissance: 15–25 teams in the field at once, 40–80 team-missions a month [E: D5]; SOG's benchmark 454 Cambodian missions in 1969 [M014·S3]
- Replacement: about 30–50 operators a year from selection and the six-month OTC [E: S1]
- 2026 equipment stock about two to three years of wastage; thinning from 1966–68 [E: D8]
- History's benchmarks: JPRC never recovered an American POW (8 and 9 successes in 1968–69, 272 Vietnamese recovered) [M014·S6]; Son Tay empty, prisoners moved 14 July 1970 [M014·S5]; SOG's northern agents more than three-quarters captured [M014·S3]

**Negative specification.** Delta cannot find what no one has found. It finishes targets that the combined task force, the U-2S and Global Hawks, a defector or a captured document have located [M012] [M003]; it locates very little itself beyond the reach of its own patrols, and nothing under triple canopy from the air. It cannot destroy a main-force unit: a battalion of 400 is not a raid target for a troop of 20–24 operators [E: D2]. It cannot reach COSVN by raid while COSVN is in Cambodia, because no American ground force crosses that border until September 1967, and then only on reconnaissance on foot without air support, and with no exploitation force [M014·S3]; and COSVN, about 2,400 staff dispersed and mobile, evaded Junction City, Menu and the 1970 incursion [M014·S7]. It cannot raid the North before history's one raid at Son Tay in November 1970 [M014·S5]. It cannot enter Laos before October 1965 [M014·S3]. It brings no 160th SOAR and no drone orbit of its own [U]: its lift is a company of light helicopters [M014·S2], and any operation larger than a troop or deeper than their range needs the theater's lift. It cannot speak Vietnamese, so every target that comes through Vietnamese hands comes with the risk of a leak. It cannot be handed to the ARVN, and its 2026 equipment cannot be repaired in 1964 (D8). And it is not numerous: about 280–350 people who go on operations [E: D2], refilled at perhaps 30–50 a year.

**Denies the enemy.** It denies the enemy's senior cadre in the South the night. From 1964 a province committee member, a regional military commander or a COSVN courier who sleeps in a hamlet that the task force's files have named can be taken from his bed by men he cannot see, in 2–6 hours from the decision [E: D5]. It denies the infrastructure the comfort that only the hamlet cadre are hunted. It denies the base areas inside the South (the Iron Triangle, the Ho Bo woods, the Do Xa, the U Minh) their freedom from observation at night. It denies the Trail and the Cambodian base areas their freedom from observation from October 1965 and September 1967, within history's limits [M014·S3]. It denies Hanoi certainty that a prisoner camp in the South is beyond reach. It does not deny the enemy its main force, its sanctuaries or its strategy.

**Verdict.** Delta is the best night raid force in the world, put into a war fought at night by an enemy who believed the night was his. That is worth something real and specific: from late 1964 the senior infrastructure in the South (province committees, regional commanders, couriers and their documents) can be taken when it is found, at night, by men who see. The unit's whole value runs through the combined task force's files [M012]. Delta adds the hands for the hardest 10–20% of the task force's targets [E: D13] and the speed to reach them before they move. That will be 50–250 more senior cadre a year at maturity, against an infrastructure counted in the tens of thousands [E: D5]. It is reconnaissance that finds the Trail and the Cambodian base areas a little better than SOG did, from history's dates. It is a better POW recovery force than any history had. It does not touch the main force, the sanctuaries or Hanoi's decision. COSVN, which the provision names, is beyond its reach until 1970 and probably after, because it was a moving headquarters of 2,400 people in a country no American could enter [M014·S7]. The raid into the North that history made, the unit could make better. It is one raid. Delta is a scalpel. The war has places to use one, and it is not won with one.

**Pushes:** FIND.vci +0.04 to +0.15 [VCI neutralised a year who were on a prior target list, district level or above, thousands] by the end of P2 (low), VCI.strength -0.4 to 0 [VCI cadre in the South, thousands] by the end of P2 (low), SUBVERT.defection 0 to +0.3 [Chieu Hoi ralliers, thousands a year] by the end of P2 (low), US.casualties +5 to +25 [US killed by hostile action in the calendar year in which the phase ends (Phase I: 1965)] by the end of P2 (low), FIND.main_force 0 to +2 [% of main-force contacts the allies initiate on units already located] by the end of P2 (low), TRAIL.tonnage_arriving -4% to 0% of history's figure by the end of P2 (low), SANCT.cambodia -2 to 0 [enemy main-force battalions based in Cambodia] by the end of P4 (low), US.personnel_demand +1 to +1.5 [US military personnel in Vietnam, thousands] by the end of P2 (medium) · **Depends on:** LOG.helicopter_hours, INTEL.penetration, FIND.vci, FIND.main_force, STRIKE.responsiveness, SANCT.laos, AIR.north_defences, POP.night_control

## P014b · MACV Joint Special Operations Command (MACV-JSOC), newly formed after the Gulf of Tonkin incident: a joint headquarters under COMUSMACV that commands SFOD-D and the special operations units the user will assign to it later, with standing liaison to MACV J-2 and J-3, MACV-SOG, the CIA station, the Combined Interagency Task Force of memorandum 012, the Joint General Staff and the US Mission, for logistics, targeting and deconfliction
one headquarters, formed August 1964 [U]; ~250–450 personnel [E: D2] · spaces ~250–450 [E: a joint task force headquarters at the scale of the early JSOC of 1980–81; no ceiling (CONFIG)] · arrives 1964-08-15 · FIND, FIX, STRIKE, SUSTAIN · institutional

**Key figures.**
- Formed 15 August 1964 [E: after the Tonkin reports of 2 and 4 August]; model JSOC, 15 December 1980 [M014·S8]; precedent MACV-SOG, 24 January 1964 [M014·S3]
- Strength about 250–450, of whom 40–80 in 15–20 liaison cells [E: D2]
- Liaison with MACV J-2 and J-3, SOG, the CIA station, the combined task force [M012], the air command, the four corps (US and ARVN), the JGS, the National Police, the US Mission and Vientiane [U] [E: judgment from the period's establishments and practice]
- Capacity: 2–6 operations at once, 40–150 a month; deconfliction 1–3 hours inside the South [E: D5]
- No cross-border authority; no authority over the CIA or the GVN [M014·S3] [U]
- Running cost about $10–20 million a year in 1964 prices, excluding Delta [E: judgment from the period's establishments and practice]

**Negative specification.** The headquarters cannot authorise any cross-border operation: Laos stays with the ambassador, Cambodia with Washington from September 1967, the North with the President [M014·S3] [M014·S5]. It holds no authority over the CIA, the GVN, the JGS or the National Police; it can only ask them. It brings no units except Delta, no aviation beyond Delta's own [M014·S2], no surveillance and no sources of its own: every target it acts on comes from someone else's files [M012] [M003]. It cannot stop leaks from Vietnamese channels it must use; it can only route around them. It is not a theater command, and it cannot direct the conventional war.

**Denies the enemy.** It denies the enemy the seams between the American services, SOG, the CIA station and the combined task force, which a single raid force working through MACV J-3 would leave open: fewer raids planned through channels that leak, fewer sources burned, fewer teams shot by friendly fire.

**Verdict.** The headquarters is the price of using Delta well. Without it, Delta would work through MACV J-3 and the corps, its targets would pass through hands that leak, and its raids would collide with the task force's and SOG's. With it, a small joint staff keeps the targets in American hands, clears the ground for each raid in hours, and shares what the raids bring back. It adds nothing new to the war's knowledge. It adds speed and order to a scalpel. It is also the frame for the units the user will add later, and its value will grow or shrink with them.

**Pushes:** US.personnel_demand +0.25 to +0.45 [US military personnel in Vietnam, thousands] by the end of P1 (medium), FIND.vci 0 to +0.1 [VCI neutralised a year who were on a prior target list, district level or above, thousands] by the end of P2 (low) · **Depends on:** ADVISE.leverage, GVN.police, US.political_tolerance

## Employment concepts
EC014-1 the held-belt night lift · EC014-2 the province committee take-down · EC014-3 the base-area stake-out · EC014-4 the cross-border road watch (Laos, from October 1965) · EC014-5 the Cambodian foot reconnaissance (from September 1967) · EC014-6 the camp snatch · EC014-7 the Son Tay package. Abandoned: EC014-8 the partnered ARVN cordon (cost the surprise and put the target in a Vietnamese channel) · EC014-9 the COSVN decapitation raid (no building, no border crossing, warned by trawlers) · EC014-10 the Hanoi raid (no authority) · EC014-11 the sustained hundred-raid month (no rotation base; sustained rate 25–50 raids and 8–12 recon teams)

## Interactions
- P014a × P012b: the task force's National Fusion Centre is Delta's target deck and Delta is the task force's hardest-target arm; the task force gives the raid its file, its warrant where one is possible and its exploitation team, and Delta gives the file the province and region cadre the task force's own forces could not reach (F014-1, F014-7)
- P014a × P006a: the district centres' files are the base layer under every Delta target in the South, and a raid's documents go back into them within hours (F014-1, F014-14)
- P014a × P002a: an arrest inside the held belt runs through the Special Branch and the 72-hour magistrate review of the 1964 statute, so a night raid on a house is a police action with soldiers in it; outside the held belt there is no warrant and no review, and that boundary is where Delta's political cost lives (F014-16)
- P014a × P003a, P003b: the U-2S and Global Hawk cue a team to a place worth watching, and the team sees under the canopy the imagery cannot enter; the pairing is the only instrument in the record that reaches a point target below the trees (F014-2, F014-11)
- P014a × P005a, P005b: a team's coordinate becomes a GBU-31 aimpoint through the Tan Son Nhut cell, which makes Delta the first provision that can put the J's precision on a target under canopy (F014-11)
- P014a × P013a, P013b: Delta's one possible raid into the North flies through an air-defence system that the opening strike of 2 March 1965 broke and Moscow then rebuilt; the raid is easier in 1965 and no easier in 1970 (F014-21)
- P014b × P012a: the combined operations command's corps centres clear the ground for Delta's raids and receive its restricted operating areas; without that switchboard the deconfliction would run through four American and four ARVN corps staffs one telephone call at a time (F014-6, F014-19)
- P014b × P006c: the selected advisory corps is how MACV-JSOC learns which Vietnamese channels leak, because the adviser who has been with a counterpart eighteen months is the man who knows (F014-18)


## Standing directives

- **DIRCP01-1** · In each Part 3, take at least one causal chain from an earlier memorandum whose later links fall in a phase this memorandum revises, and test it against the war as now written; where the new provision or free play makes it resolve differently, say so in the chain review and let it (every chain in memoranda 001–005 resolved as predicted, which is more likely tidiness than foresight)
- **DIRCP01-2** · A war-wide figure for lives saved, or any war-wide count built from a rate, must be shown at work in at least two dated events in the chapters before a later memorandum repeats it; until then it is cited as a judgment resting on its rate, with the rate named (CP01 calibration of the [X-004] lives-saved figure)
- **DIRMT01-1** · In every §4.N, state the date of the Republic's fall as its own estimate, separately from the rung: a window, the mechanisms in the cumulative force that pull it earlier and those that pull it later, and which dominate and why; "on the historical timeline" may be written only as the conclusion of that test, and a change of date is reported as a change of date and does not by itself move the rung between (a) and (b) while the ladder's overlap stands (the historical fall, twenty-five months after the last American combat troops left, satisfies the words of rung (b), and seven memoranda have kept (a) and (b) apart by the date alone)
- **DIRMT01-2** · In every §4.N, carry a running sum of the sub-band estimates that all memoranda so far have made on the same variable (American dead, ARVN battalions not lost, and the like), tagged as exercise judgments with their rates named, and say whether the sum crosses a band; and treat the American aid appropriation of 1974 and the refusal of April 1975 as events a provision can change, not as history to be carried (each memorandum judged its own saving of American lives alone, and the 1974 vote was never examined)
- **DIRMT01-3** · Where a chapter's end vector returns a variable to the historical state from a non-zero band in the phase before, the chapter must contain the dated events that produce the convergence; and in every memorandum that revises Phase VI, state in the phase's analysis the Republic's state at the end of 1974, before the last offensive, because the phase's end vector is measured after the fall and cannot record anything the fall erased (Phase V returned four countryside variables to history with no sentence on the countryside, and Phase VI's vector is blind by construction)
- **DIRMT01-4** · Where a memorandum alters an event and keeps its historical outcome, name what absorbs the difference (the enemy's choice to bypass or decline, a decision above the level the provision reached, an external fixed by law or by another government) and show it in the event; "as historically" is a conclusion, never a mechanism (in Phase VI at least six altered events in the last campaign restore the historical outcome by statement)
- **DIRMT01-5** · Where a perverse effect or a capture undoes a gain, state the net in both directions with its weight, and where several provisions' institutions fall to the same mechanism in the same years, judge them together before judging each alone (four institutions from four memoranda fall to the lapse of the American lever in 1970–71, each judged alone, and every memorandum closes on the gain undone)
- **DIRMT01-6** · The next memorandum or review whose Part 3 revises Phase V or VI states the PAVN's 1972 losses in this war against the historical figure and the rebuilding time that follows, before writing 1973–75 (memorandum 005 made the measured sieges the enemy's worst battles; Phase V keeps the historical losses and Phase VI the historical rebuilding)
- **DIRMT01-7** · Every memorandum whose Part 3 revises Phase V or VI tests its effects against the critical path of 1975 (the palace's orders of 13–14 March, the 1st Corps' march against the rains, and Minh's surrender) and states whether any mechanism could delay the collapse of I and II Corps by about three weeks, the threshold beyond which the assault falls into the rains; effects on fights the PAVN could bypass are reported as such (the date of the fall was carried for seven memoranda without its critical path ever being stated)
- **DIRMT01-8** · Every memorandum touching the countryside states its effect separately for the Delta, the coastal lowlands of I and II Corps, the Highlands and their peoples, and the Saigon belt, and names a place in each where the effect is shown or says why there is none (the Delta was written as a footnote, the Montagnards appear twice and FULRO never, and Binh Dinh vanished from the record after 1967)
- **DIRMT01-9** · Every provision touching the reliability of the ARVN or the territorial forces addresses the soldier's family: where it lives, what his pay buys after inflation, and what happens to it when the unit moves or the front gives way (the corps of 1975 dissolved toward their families, and no memorandum had treated them)
- **DIRMT01-10** · The enemy's decisions have authors: in each memorandum name the body or commander who took the enemy's decision of G3, and distinguish Hanoi, the B-2 Front and COSVN, and the regional fronts where they differed; treat the Soviet and Chinese supply as variables with their own politics (COSVN vanishes from the record after 1971, the Phuoc Long argument is told as one mind, and the Soviet deliveries of 1974 are absent)
- **DIRMT01-11** · Every memorandum touching the countryside or the RVNAF states its effect on rice (production, procurement and the Front's take) and on the piaster and the soldier's pay, with at least one dated event (rice appears eleven times in Phase II and once in 1972–75, the years the economy decided)
- **DIRCP02-1** · At each checkpoint, consolidate a chapter over the limit in two steps: first merge minor historical events into summary events, then merge each memorandum's own minor NEW events in that phase into one summary per memorandum, keeping every fact a later memorandum or position cites by event number; and every memorandum's §4 adds to a phase's overview and ending only one paragraph, replacing rather than appending where an earlier memorandum's paragraph states the same variable (CP02 consolidation of P1 and P2, still about 7,600 and 9,300 words over the limit after the first step)
- **DIRCP02-2** · In each Part 3 the chain taken under DIRCP01-1 must be one written by another memorandum whose terminal event this memorandum did not write; C006-4, whose terminal link no chapter carries, is the first such chain for any memorandum revising Phase V (17 of 19 chains in memoranda 006–010 resolved as their authors predicted)
- **DIRCP02-3** · Where a provision acts on a variable already at the cap of the bands in a phase, the memorandum states its increment in the running sum of DIRMT01-2 with the factors it multiplies and how they overlap, and names the target the enemy moves to in answer (POSCP02-2); a product of overlapping judgments is reported as a range with its upper bound marked (CP02 calibration of the battalions-not-broken figure)
- **DIRR01-1** · DIRCP02-3's rule for a variable "already at the cap of the bands" lapses, because the scale has no cap short of a different war: a provision that acts on such a variable re-judges its range, and the range of the facet it acts on, and the running sums of DIRMT01-2 now say which part of that range they support rather than whether they cross a band; the rest of DIRCP02-3 stands, the target the enemy moves to in answer is still named, and a product of overlapping judgments is still reported as a range with its upper bound marked (the user's change of scale, 24 Nov 2026; R01)
- **DIRR01-2** · A range marked "converted" is the old band restated, not a judgment: it is never cited as a judgment of the war, and every memorandum or checkpoint whose evidence bears on a converted entry, or on one of the four entries converted from the cap, re-judges it with a confidence and a note (R01's mechanical conversion of the end vectors)
- **DIRR01-3** · Where a variable has facets, §2 names the facet a provision acts on, and every revised phase that judges a facet names the parent's binding facet and says why it binds; the parent is never the average of its facets, and a gain on one facet is not reported as a gain on the parent unless the binding facet moved (the user's point of 24 Nov 2026 that "ARVN effectiveness" does not discriminate between urban combat, combined arms, anti-armor and the rest)
- **DIRR02-1** · A study describes the war and never changes it: no study adds, alters or cancels an event or moves the end state, and where a study finds the record inconsistent it records a question for an erratum or a checkpoint rather than settling it (the user's design of 24 Nov 2026; R02)
- **DIRR02-2** · Every memorandum whose variables a study covers is written against that study: Part 2 judges its pushes against the study's values and says plainly when the provision's effect contradicts the study and which should give way, and Part 3 records what changed in the area in the study's entry (R02)
- **DIRR02-3** · A study's value is never cited as a measurement: study values are exercise judgments on the R01 scale, an indicator a study gives carries its own provenance, and a figure the study generates carries the X-tag of its study run (X-ST01 and so on) forever (A13a; R02)
- **DIRR03-1** · Every value and every push is written in its variable's natural unit (schema/VARIABLES.toml, v1.0.8): this war's figure beside history's where history's is known, otherwise the difference from history in the unit or as a percentage of history's figure, and a note that says what the figure means on the ground; a claim that cannot be put in its unit is not yet a judgment (the user's ruling of 25 Nov 2026 that the −10..+10 scale is meaningless; R03)
- **DIRR03-2** · A memorandum or checkpoint that judges a headline entry researches history's figure for it where it can and enters `hist` and `src`; an `[E: basis]` estimate of history's figure is allowed with its basis stated, and an unresearched figure is never stated from memory (R03; CLAUDE.md "read; never recall")
- **DIRR03-3** · A memorandum re-judges, in units, every unjudged headline entry among its own dependencies when its evidence bears on it, not only the variables it pushes (CP03 §3: night control sat converted through three memoranda that broke the infrastructure it depends on)
- **DIRCP03-1** · A dedicated consolidation run brings Phases I and II under the chapter limit before the next checkpoint: minor events merged into summary events by the CANCELLED/NEW rule, per-memorandum paragraphs merged by subject, every fact a later memorandum or position relies on kept, and successive restatements of one figure given once with its parts (CP03 §2: Phase III's three restatements of the first phase's dead)
- **DIRCP03-2** · A push or judgment on enemy strength (PAVN.strength_south, VC.main_force, VC.local_force) names the formations it moves and by how many months, and is tested against the chapters' order of battle before it is entered (CP03 §5: memorandum 013's divisions held at home)
- **DIRCP03-3** · A memorandum that improves FIND.vci states what the improvement tells the allies about the enemy's main forces and the timing of their offensives, and what it does not; files on the political organisation warn of where, not when (POSCP03-2)

## Settled positions on this memorandum's variables

- **POSTNA-2** · vars: POP.night_control, RFPF.effectiveness · Night control of a hamlet is held only by security resident in it with a means of calling help and a reaction that arrives in the dark; mobile forces that leave at dusk do not change it (TNA G-2)
- **POSTNA-3** · vars: ENEMY.engagement_control, ENEMY.regeneration, SANCT.laos, SANCT.cambodia · While the enemy controls whether to accept battle and regenerates in sanctuary, attrition has no crossover point; a strategy that waits for one waits for something the geometry does not permit (TNA G-8)
- **POSTNA-4** · vars: TRAIL.capacity, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving · On the opening date the enemy's external requirement from the North is of the order of 20 tons a day against a Trail of 20–30 tons a day and an uncounted sea route; Trail capacity is elastic with labour, so interdiction is judged only by tonnage arriving below the requirement, never by trucks or porters destroyed (TNA G-9)
- **POSTNA-5** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.credibility_gap, US.casualties · The American political clock is spent by casualties, cost and time, and fastest by the discovery that reported progress was false; a provision that improves a metric without improving the war shortens the clock (TNA G-5, G-10)
- **POSTNA-6** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, POP.gvn_legitimacy · Advisory leverage trades short-run effectiveness against long-run legitimacy; no position on that line is free, and every proposal to increase leverage states what it costs the Republic's claim to be its own government (TNA G-6)
- **POS001-1** · vars: POP.land_tenure, POP.gvn_legitimacy, POP.night_control · Land reform changes what the government's arrival means, not whether it arrives: its value in any hamlet equals the night security behind it, and titles issued are never evidence of allegiance (001 §2 F001-4, F001-10; §4.P2)
- **POS001-2** · vars: GVN.corruption, ADVISE.leverage, GVN.political_stability · An independent anti-corruption body in the Republic survives only with a Vietnamese patron and an American lever; its durable effect is on muster, pay and documentary cases below the top, and its reach upward ends when the lever lapses with the American drawdown (001 §4.P4)
- **POS001-4** · vars: POP.gvn_legitimacy, VCI.strength · A one-band gain in the countryside's allegiance does not carry into the conventional battles of 1972 and 1975; the end state turns on the military balance after the American withdrawal, and political gains are necessary but not sufficient to move it (001 §4.N)
- **POS002-1** · vars: GVN.police, FIND.vci, POP.night_control · A rural police and Special Branch attack the infrastructure, not the main force; their value in any village equals the night security beside them, and where they work best their arrest count falls, so arrest counts and quotas are never the measure of them (002 F002-11, F002-17; §4.P2)
- **POS002-2** · vars: GVN.admin_capacity, ADVISE.leverage, GVN.political_stability · Merit selection of province and district chiefs survives the coups only with the American aid lever behind it; when the lever lapses with the drawdown the President captures the Board without abolishing it, and its durable gain is the chiefs' experience below the palace (002 §4.P4, EV002-6)
- **POS002-3** · vars: GVN.police, GVN.political_stability, POP.gvn_legitimacy · A stronger and better-recorded police in a coup-prone state is used by the government of the day against its domestic opposition, and its records are a list of loyalties the enemy can capture; both costs are paid and do not outweigh the gain in the held belt (002 F002-9, F002-16; §4.P2, §4.P3)
- **POS003-1** · vars: FIND.main_force, FIX.capability, STRIKE.responsiveness · Airborne radar and signals reconnaissance find the enemy's movement in the open and his headquarters' transmitters, never his regiments under canopy; their value in any engagement equals what can be put on a track within the hour, and an improvement in finding is never claimed as an improvement in fixing (003 §2 F003-5; §4.P2–P5)
- **POS003-2** · vars: INFIL.sea, SANCT.cambodia, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving · In this war the sea route to the South's coast closed in 1964 under observation and the enemy's southern supply moved to Sihanoukville from June 1965; supply through Cambodia, not by sea, is the principal external line into III and IV Corps from 1965 until Lon Nol's coup (003 §2 F003-3; EV003-2)
- **POS003-3** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.credibility_gap · In this war no attack of 4 August 1964 was claimed and Pierce Arrow was not flown; the Southeast Asia Resolution rests on the attack of 2 August, and the Tonkin deception is not part of the credibility gap in any later phase (003 §4.P1, §4.P3; EV000-3)
- **POS004-1** · vars: RFPF.effectiveness, POP.night_control, ENEMY.engagement_control · Infantry small arms change how the fights the enemy accepts go, never which fights he accepts; at the outpost their value equals the platoon's presence after dark and the reaction behind it, and the enemy's answer to a better-armed post is to attack what is not rearmed (004 F004-1, F004-3, F004-16; §4.P1)
- **POS004-2** · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, US.unit_quality, US.political_tolerance · In this war the ARVN and the RF/PF carry modern carbines from 1964, and the 1967 M16 crisis and inquiry and the 1968–69 rearmament do not occur; from 1969 the historical army has caught up, and the remaining difference is the squad gun, the marksman and the practice (004 F004-6; §4.P2–P4)
- **POS005-1** · vars: STRIKE.responsiveness, FIND.main_force, FIX.capability · GPS weapons change what dies at a measured coordinate, never what can be located; in this war the J's precision is decisive where the enemy holds still long enough to be measured, at the siege and the fixed crossing, and adds nothing against the main force under canopy or the infrastructure in the hamlets (005 §2 F005-1, F005-7, F005-21)
- **POS005-2** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, FIX.capability, US.political_tolerance · In this war the defence of besieged positions from 1965 rests on the B-52J and an American coordinate cell; it is far stronger while American air power is present and leaves the RVNAF more dependent on it when it goes (005 §2 F005-20)
- **POS005-4** · vars: TRAIL.capacity, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving · In this war the panhandle's fixed crossings were cut by the B-52J from April 1966, and Group 559 rebuilt the net as braided fords, causeways and pontoons with no single point of failure; from 1966 the Trail is more redundant than history's, and precision strikes on crossings are never counted as reductions in tonnage arriving (005 §4.P2; EV005-2, EV000-55)
- **POSCP01-1** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.credibility_gap · The small gains on the American clock in memoranda 001–005 (no Tonkin deception, honest damage assessment, no M16 scandal, a conviction in 1967, fewer prisoners and no Bach Mai in 1972) narrow the credibility gap and do not move tolerance by a band in any phase, because the clock was spent by the casualties of 1965–68 and by Tet, which no provision changed and one made sharper (CP01 §3; C003-3)
- **POSCP01-2** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · In this war the American lever was used to protect the Republic's honest institutions from its own governments and never to make the Republic own the instruments of the conventional war (coordinates, reconnaissance, guided weapons, ammunition stocks); the dependence deepened by memoranda 004 and 005 was never contested by the instrument that could have contested it (CP01 §3)
- **POS006-1** · vars: FIND.vci, VCI.strength, POP.night_control · Phung Hoang adds the layer above the hamlet to what the Special Branch knows, only where the night is held; outside the held belt it is the historical Phoenix whatever its rules, and its audited count, which falls where it works best, is the measure, never its arrest count (006 F006-15, F006-18, F006-26)
- **POS006-2** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.casualties, ENEMY.engagement_control · Unit rotation makes the American battalion fight better in the contacts it gets and changes neither which contacts it gets nor the late-war breakdown of discipline; it gives the enemy a relief window to aim at, and it does not prevent atrocity (006 F006-6, F006-16, F006-19)
- **POS006-3** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · The selected advisory corps deepens influence, not authority; its durable values are continuity across the American unit's relief and honest reporting, and a better adviser deepens the advised unit's dependence on American fire unless he hands over the radio, which works for artillery, the VNAF and medevac and not for the B-52J (006 F006-2, F006-17, F006-23)
- **POS006-4** · vars: FIND.vci, INTEL.penetration, GVN.political_stability · In this war the national Phung Hoang file, built to warrant standard from 1964, was moved into the Central Intelligence Organization in 1970, consolidated in one building for the 1971 election, and captured intact on 30 April 1975 with the I Corps files a month earlier; the accuracy that made it valuable to the Republic made it more valuable to the victors (006 §4.P4, §4.P6; EV002-6, EV000-94, EV000-98)
- **POS006-5** · vars: FIND.vci, US.credibility_gap · In this war there was no ICEX, no Phoenix quota and no 1969 discovery of false claims; the attack on the infrastructure had an audited count from 1965, and "Phoenix" became a press scandal in March 1967 over the Duc Thanh raid rather than in 1970 over the programme (006 §4.P2, §4.P3; EV006-4, EV000-54)
- **POS006-6** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.casualties, US.personnel_demand · In this war American battalions deploy, are relieved and withdraw as units; the estimated saving of 1,000–2,000 American lives in 1966–69 is a judgment on a rate of 3–6 percent shown so far only at Dien Ban, and does not move the casualty band (006 §4.P2, §4.H; EV006-3)
- **POS007-2** · vars: ARVN.leadership, ADVISE.leverage, GVN.political_stability · The ranked list for generals and division commands works only while the American aid condition protects it; in this war it filled one or two division commands in ten against the palace's preference by 1967, became advisory on 12 January 1970, and never governed the corps, so that the decisive commands of 1972 and 1975 were chosen as they were historically (007 §4.P4, §4.P5; EV007-4, EV007-5)
- **POS007-3** · vars: GVN.political_stability, ARVN.leadership, INTEL.penetration · An educated field-grade officer corps whose promotion is blocked at the top becomes a faction in the palace's eyes; in this war the colonels' petition of September 1970 was answered by moving about forty regimental and battalion commanders out of the field before Lam Son 719, and COSVN targeted the passed-over officers from 1968 with small yield (007 §4.P3, §4.P4; EV007-5, EV000-52)
- **POS007-4** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.casualties, POP.civilian_harm · American officer education from 1957 improves platoon and company leadership and saves American lives at a rate of perhaps one to three percent of small-unit deaths in 1965–69, below a band; it does not prevent My Lai or the late-war decay of discipline, which came from the command climate above the lieutenant (007 §4.P2, §4.P3; EV000-23)
- **POSMT01-1** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, VNAF.capability, ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.leadership · Rung (a) is reaffirmed after seven memoranda on its mechanism, not its date: every provision so far is American-owned and withdrawn by 1973, or works below the level of command at which 1972 and 1975 were decided, or was captured by the palace when the American lever lapsed in 1970–71; the rung will not move until a provision reaches an air arm the Republic owns, sustainment that survives the 1974 appropriation, or the choice of the corps commanders (MT01 M-12)
- **POSMT01-4** · vars: POP.night_control, VCI.strength, POP.gvn_legitimacy, FIND.vci · The countryside at the end of 1972 is not history's: where a PAVN division sat in the peopled lowlands (northern Binh Dinh, Quang Tri) the gains of 1964–71 were lost, while the held belt of the Delta and the Saigon region kept its posts and files and stays one band better at night and against the infrastructure; the government's legitimacy returns to history's through the decrees of 1972 (MT01 M-4; EVMT01-1, EVMT01-2, EVMT01-3)
- **POSMT01-5** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.casualties, US.credibility_gap · The sum of the American lives the provisions saved is a judgment of about 2,500–5,000, mostly in 1965–69, five to nine percent of the historical dead, below a band; it does not move tolerance, and the changes in the record that bear on the 1974 appropriation roughly cancel, so the vote stands as history's until a provision changes what the Republic needs Congress to pay for (MT01 M-7; EV000-89)
- **POS008-1** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, ADVISE.leverage, US.political_tolerance · A domestic arsenal, battery works and rebuild depot stretch the aid dollar in 1974–75 only if the RVNAF has been made to buy from them while American supply was free; this headquarters adopts a domestic share enforced by the Aid Compliance Board from 1965, and the stretch changes what the fiscal 1975 appropriation buys, not the vote (008 §2 F008-2, F008-20, F008-23)
- **POS008-2** · vars: POP.night_control, RFPF.effectiveness, STRIKE.responsiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · A radio kept on the air at the post supplies the means of calling help in POSTNA-2 and moves the post's binding constraint to the reaction and fire within range; the Front answers by attacking the relief and the posts that cannot call, and the radio's gain appears as attacks not made (008 §2 F008-1, F008-3, F008-6, F008-16)
- **POS008-3** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, US.political_tolerance, HANOI.will · In this war the Republic's own arsenal and battery works stretched the fiscal 1975 appropriation to about $850 million–$1 billion of history's and kept its ammunition and communications from going dark in 1974, but delayed the collapse of I and II Corps by days, not the three weeks that would have moved the date; domestic sustainment without an air arm the Republic owns and a choice of corps commanders does not move the rung (008 §4.P6, §4.N; EV000-89, EVMT01-4)
- **POS008-4** · vars: RFPF.effectiveness, POP.night_control, STRIKE.responsiveness · From 1967 the territorial post's first call is for fire, not men, after the Front's ambush of the relief at My Phuoc Tay; this makes the post cheaper to hold and keeps the platoon behind its wire, so that the post is held better and the hamlet outside it is not, and the call passes to Vietnamese district guns in 1970–71 (008 §4.P2, §4.P4; EV008-4, EV008-7)
- **POS008-5** · vars: GVN.corruption, ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · The Directorate of Defence Industry fell to the palace in February 1970 with the four other institutions built behind the American lever; its output and the domestic share survived because the Joint General Staff wanted them, and honest lot acceptance did not, costing perhaps a tenth to a fifth of the base's 1974 value (008 §4.P4; EV002-6)
- **POS009-2** · vars: MED.survival, US.casualties, US.political_tolerance · In this war every soldier of both armies is taught the tourniquet in basic training; the saving is a judgment on a rate of two to four percent of killed in action, shown at Albany and in the first wave of Tet, about 900–1,900 Americans and 4,000–12,000 South Vietnamese, below a band on every variable and proof against enemy adaptation (009 §4.P2, §4.P3, §4.N; EV000-23, EV000-42)
- **POS009-3** · vars: ARVN.desertion, ECON.inflation, VCI.strength · Training does not reach desertion, which follows the soldier's pay, rice and family; the trained deserter carries the course home, and a few hundred a year in the Saigon belt carry it to the Front's guerrillas (009 §4.P2; EV009-3)
- **POS010-2** · vars: ARVN.leadership, ADVISE.leverage, GVN.political_stability · The NCO promotion gate is a Vietnamese rule enforced by the training command and the boards below colonel; it was broken by the National Day decree of 1 November 1970 and repaired within a year by barring the next promotion, and it is the one merit rule of 1964 that survived the lapse of the American lever, because it threatened no one the palace cared about (010 EV010-6, F010-5)
- **POS010-3** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.casualties, US.personnel_demand · American NCO education from 1957 makes the American squad better in the patrol base and the night ambush and saves about 300–900 American lives, a judgment on a rate of one to three percent of small-unit deaths, below a band; it costs the senior NCOs of 1966–67 and does not prevent the decay of 1969–71 (010 F010-12, F010-18, F010-22; EV010-2, EV010-5)
- **POS010-4** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, STRIKE.responsiveness · The American NCO course carries the habit of fixing the enemy and calling fire down to the ARVN squad; it is a strength the Republic owns only where the gun at the other end is Vietnamese, as at Long My, and a dependence everywhere else (010 F010-24; EV008-7)
- **POSCP02-2** · vars: ENEMY.engagement_control, POP.civilian_harm, VCI.strength · Every provision since 004 that improved the RVNAF below the company was answered by the enemy moving his war to what the provision did not reach: the relief, the borrowed district, the mine in the hamlet, the untrained self-defence group; the provisions' gain in the army is paid for in part by the unprotected population, and every later provision touching the army or the posts names the target the enemy moves to and estimates the cost there (CP02 §1, §6; EV008-4, EV009-2, EV009-4, EV010-4)
- **POSCP02-3** · vars: US.personnel_demand, US.unit_quality · Unit rotation's overlap, the selected advisory corps, the drill-sergeant cadre and the NCO schools draw on one pool of experienced American senior NCOs in 1965–67; the shortage of sergeants first class comes three to six months early and runs deeper in 1967, and against a ceiling of none it changes no battle; it is the American counterpart of POSCP01-3 and is cited whenever a provision adds American senior NCOs out of the line (CP02 §3; F010-11, F010-12)
- **POS011-1** · vars: US.political_tolerance, NEGOT.position · In this war there is no Watergate: Nixon serves to January 1977, the Senate hearings, the Saturday Night Massacre, impeachment and resignation never happen, and the War Powers override fails; Case–Church still passes in June 1973 by veto-proof margins, so the end of American combat in Indochina on 15 August 1973 is law, and the binding constraint on American support from 1973 is Congress, not the President (011 F011-7, F011-9; EV000-86)
- **POS011-2** · vars: US.political_tolerance, ARVN.self_sufficiency · American military aid to the RVNAF is about $950 million for fiscal 1975, buying through the domestic stretch about what $1.2 billion bought historically, with supplementals of about $150 million in March and $175 million in May 1975 and about $800 million for fiscal 1976; the money reached fuel, aircraft and heavy rounds and saved perhaps 1,500–4,000 of the Republic's dead in 1974, and it never reached the soldier's pay or the artillery duel with the 130mm (011 F011-2, F011-21; EV000-89, EV000-91, EV011-2, EV000-97, EV011-3)
- **POS011-5** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.political_tolerance, US.casualties · A quarter of the historically inducted enlisted voluntarily in the same jobs (Reading A); draft calls are a quarter smaller and the force is unchanged; the volunteers die at the draftees' rate and are about half as likely to be on the drug and refusal lists of 1970–71, with no change to any battle (011 F011-15, F011-19; EV010-5)
- **REV011-2** · reverses POSMT01-5 · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.casualties, US.credibility_gap · The sum of the American lives saved stands at about 3,700–7,800 and does not move tolerance. What is reversed is the vote: the fiscal 1975 appropriation is no longer history's, because the President who fought for it was not fighting impeachment, and the April 1975 request is Nixon's and partly voted (011 F011-17; EV000-89, EV000-97)
- **POS012-1** · vars: VCI.strength, FIND.vci, POP.night_control · In this war a combined interagency task force with lift, raid teams and cross-province warrants from 1964 broke the Front's district government of the held belt from its edge in 1965–67, about a third to a half of the district layer in 12–18 provinces beyond what the police and the district centres had done; it reached committees beyond the held belt only as far as helicopter and warrant, never into the base areas, and its gains hold only where the posts hold the night (012 F012-27; EV012-4)
- **POS012-2** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.leadership, GVN.political_stability · In this war COMUSMACV held operational control of the ARVN corps from 1964 as combined commander, exercised through the prime minister's office after Khanh's coup and over corps commanders the palace chose; it was more than coordination and less than command, and it ended in fact with the American divisions and the American lever (012 EV012-1, EV012-6)
- **POS013-1** · vars: AIR.north_effect, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving, HANOI.will · In this war the air campaign against the North was run from Saigon from 2 March 1965 on the theater's own list, without zones around Hanoi or Haiphong and without pauses, and opened with a strike that destroyed the North's power, bulk fuel, great bridges, jet base and Haiphong's cranes in a week; it did not reduce the flow to the South beyond the record's trace, and it did not move Hanoi's will; the restrictions on bombing the North were never the war's binding constraint (013 F013-7, F013-18; EV013-1, EV013-3)
- **POS013-2** · vars: NEGOT.position, US.political_tolerance · In this war there was no partial halt on 31 March 1968; the Paris talks opened on 13 November 1968, after the full halt of 1 November on history's date, and the four-party conference met in January 1969 as historically; the six months' delay cost the settlement nothing (013 F013-10; EV000-45, EV000-48, EV000-53)
- **POS013-3** · vars: AIR.losses, AIR.north_defences · In this war Rolling Thunder lost about 810–880 aircraft over or near the North rather than 922: about 30–60 fewer in 1965, 40–90 fewer in 1966–67 and 30–40 more in the summer of 1968 over Hanoi; the VPAF fought from Chinese airfields from 1965, and Bolo destroyed three MiG-21s rather than seven (013 F013-17, F013-18; EV000-53, EVCP02-4)
- **POSCP03-1** · vars: STRIKE.responsiveness, PAVN.strength_south, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving · The unrestricted opening of the air war against the North in March 1965 disrupted the North's economy, air force and alliances more than any other act of the war and did not reach the war in the South: the South's needs were small, carried through Laos by labour, and the North replaced fuel and power with drums and diesels in a season, while the trucks Moscow sent in place of heavy plant went to the Trail (POSTNA-4, C013-1). The divisions held at home in 1965 were the North's home-defence divisions on history's course too, and no formation reaches the South late by more than weeks (CP03 §5, the user's question of 25 Nov 2026)
- **POSCP03-2** · vars: FIND.vci, ENEMY.engagement_control · A picture of the enemy's political organisation warns of where his political apparatus will act and not of when or in what strength his main forces will; at Tet 1968 the files held the caches, committees and guides of the uprising, the combined estimate read them as local, and MACV's judgment of the main effort and the Joint General Staff's leave order absorbed the warning, so the surprise was national and the change was confined to the corps centres of III and IV Corps (EV000-42, EV012-8; the user's question of 25 Nov 2026)
- **POSCP03-3** · vars: POP.night_control, VCI.strength, FIND.vci · Night control judged by corps in units for the first time: the land, the police, the posts and the task force hold about 8–14 points more of III Corps' and 6–12 points more of IV Corps' rural people after dark than history's by the end of 1967, about six months to a year ahead of history's pacification there, and about 3–9 points more at the end of 1974; I and II Corps never move more than a few points, and those two corps decided 1972 and 1975 (CP03 §8; the user's question of 25 Nov 2026)

- **Robert E. Lindqvist** · Colonel, US Army; chief of the American advisory cell to the Officer Selection Board from 1964 · invented in 007 · Built the evaluation system's trainers' course at Fort Benning; estimated in 1966 that half the sale of commands had ended and half had changed its name

- **Tran Van Tra** · Lieutenant General, commander of the B-2 Front · HIST · In this war won the argument for Phuoc Long against a more cautious Politburo, and lost the argument of 31 March 1975 for a thrust on Saigon in May

- **Huynh Cong Tri** · Major, district chief of Long My, Chuong Thien, from 1966, a list chief · invented in MT01 · Took the call for fire into Vietnamese hands with the district's gun platoon in 1970–71; kept all forty-one of his posts through the offensive of 1972 and lost the road to Vi Thanh for seven weeks
- **Dao Van Luong** · Major, district chief of Hoai Nhon, Binh Dinh, from 1966 · invented in MT01 · Burned the Bong Son Special Branch files on 22 April 1972, three hours before the town fell to the PAVN 3rd Division
- **Vuong Dinh Toan** · Director of Defence Industry 1 January 1964 – February 1970, a metallurgist trained at the École Centrale who built the Bien Hoa melt shop · invented in 008 · Ran the Directorate through the domestic share, the Da Nhim towers and the Phu Cat lot; replaced by a general of the President's staff in February 1970
- **Howard B. Teague** · Colonel, US Army Ordnance Corps; chief of the advisory element to the Directorate of Defence Industry from 1964 · invented in 008 · Proposed in November 1964 the domestic share that the Aid Compliance Board adopted on 1 March 1965
- **Le Van Muoi** · Sergeant, commander of the PF platoon at the Ap My Loi post, My Phuoc Tay, Cai Lay, Dinh Tuong · invented in 008 · Called the district on the night of 9 March 1967; his post held every attack for the rest of the war

- **Daniel R. Kearsley** · Major, US Army, Selected Advisory Corps; subsector adviser of Long My, Chuong Thien, 1969–71 · invented in 008 · Handed the call for fire to the district's territorial gun platoon in 1970–71 and listened without speaking
- **Le Duan** · First Secretary of the Workers' Party of Vietnam · HIST · In this war cut back the autumn raids of 1974 and on 25–31 March 1975 put the offensive on Saigon back to the dry season of 1975–76
- **Tran Van Hai** · Sergeant Major, senior drill sergeant of the drill-sergeant academy at the Quang Trung Training Center from 1957, a member of its first class · invented in 009 · Trained the drill sergeants of the ten-week course and kept the rule that a recruit takes his orders from a Vietnamese
- **Raymond F. Coyle** · Lieutenant Colonel, US Army; chief of the MACV advisory detachment to the Central Training Command 1964–67 · invented in 009 · Watched and scored the centres and did not teach; backed the refusal of June 1964 to return a third of the drill sergeants to the battalions

- **William H. Rourke** · Master Sergeant, US Army; senior NCO adviser to the Dong De academy from 1963, a Korean War platoon sergeant · invented in 010 · Advised the Vietnamese faculty rather than teaching; his successor left in March 1971 and reported the course taught as he had found it
- **Nguyen Van Thuoc** · Master Sergeant, first sergeant of the 2nd Company, 4th Vietnamese Marine Battalion, in 1964 · invented in 010 · Took the company when its captain fell at Binh Gia on 31 December 1964 and brought it back to the perimeter by bounds
- **Tran Van Loc** · Sergeant First Class, later Master Sergeant, senior platoon sergeant of a company of the 3rd Battalion, 11th Regiment, 7th Division · invented in 010 · Held the company at Hau My on 16 November 1966 after its officers fell and called the Cai Be battery onto the tree line in eleven minutes
- **Nguyen Huu Tam** · Captain, commanding a company of the 3rd Battalion, 11th Regiment, 7th Division, in 1966 · invented in 010 · Wounded in the first minutes of the ambush at Hau My; returned to the battalion in March 1967
- **Raymond L. Ochoa** · Staff Sergeant, US Army; platoon sergeant in a battalion of the 196th Infantry Brigade at LZ Baldy in 1970 · invented in 010 · Took four men off the line for heroin and was wounded by a grenade rolled under his bunk on 14 March 1970
- **Phan Van Huong** · Brigadier General, chief of the Central Training Command in 1970–71 · invented in 010 · Ruled on 20 November 1970 that no man promoted by the National Day decree could rise again without his course

- **Richard M. Nixon** · President of the United States, January 1969 – January 1977 · HIST · In this war never touched by Watergate; fought for the fiscal 1975 appropriation, asked Congress on 7 January 1975 for money and for authority to use air power, and on 10 April 1975 for $400 million more
- **Nguyen Van Thieu** · President of the Republic of Vietnam · HIST · Refused the Dalat study on 11 March 1975 and gave no withdrawal order on 13–14 March; did not resign; took the study's method for SOUTHERN WALL in May 1975
- **Ngo Quang Truong** · Lieutenant General, commander of I Corps 1972–75 · HIST · Held I Corps in March–April 1975 on a plan that moved the soldiers' families first; withdrew Hue in order on 14–18 April and held Da Nang until SOUTHERN WALL
- **Cao Van Vien** · General, Chief of the Joint General Staff · HIST · Presented the Dalat study to Thieu on 11 March 1975 and sent it back on 6 May as a plan for the defence of Saigon

Garvin** · Major, US Army Special Forces, commander of the task force's III Corps task group 1964–66 · invented in 012 · Ran DRY SEASON, which found nothing for two months and then broke the Can Giuoc security section, and FOLLOW THROUGH, which took the region finance section's ledger at Phu Hoa Dong
- **Nguyen Huu Phuoc** · Captain, then Lieutenant Colonel, Police Special Branch, deputy of the III Corps task group 1964–66 · invented in 012 · Received Ba Lien at Tan An at 0710 on 6 October 1964; held the Special Branch's veto over the task group's raids
- **Harold J. Beck** · Lieutenant Colonel, US Army, commander of the task force's II Corps task group 1965–66 · invented in 012 · Adopted the 64-name list on the II Corps coast, which killed a family at Hoa Thanh and was ended on 2 April 1966
- **Nguyen Van Tu** · Secretary of the Hoc Mon district committee · invented in 012 · Escaped STILL WATER and FOLLOW THROUGH and governed Hoc Mon from the Ho Bo woods from January 1966

## Trajectory Log — last 5 entries

## CP02 — Checkpoint

Checkpoint CP02 reviewed memoranda 006–010, which improved the Republic's army from the private to the battalion commander, and its posts and factories. The war is better at its floor and unchanged at its ceiling. ARVN battalions broken in 1966–67 are two-fifths to a half fewer than history's, the posts of the held belt keep their routine and are passed by an enemy who reads their manuals, and the enemy moves his war to what no provision reached: the relief, the mine, the self-defence group. Nothing reached who commands the corps, the fire the Republic owns, or the soldier's pay and family, which decided 1975. Eleven historical events in Phases I and II were consolidated into four, and three coherence fixes were made in Phase II. Seventeen of nineteen chains resolved as their authors predicted. Rung (a) stands; Saigon falls on 30 April 1975.

## Memo 011 — American Political Tolerance Package: the Watergate break-in never happens, a quarter of the historical draftees serve as volunteers, and the My Lai massacre does not happen

Memorandum 011 changed the war from Washington. In this war the Watergate burglary never happened, a quarter of the draftees volunteered, and nobody was killed at Son My. The volunteers and the missing massacre quieted the draft and the courtrooms of 1966–71 without changing the public's verdict or any battle. The removal of Watergate did what ten theater provisions could not: it reached the level at which the war was lost. Case–Church passed anyway, and no bomber returned. But a President who did not resign got the Republic about $950 million for fiscal 1975 instead of $700 million, with fuel and aircraft, and after Phuoc Long he asked Congress for more. Thieu, holding that money and that promise, refused on 11–14 March 1975 to give anything up. The Highlands fell after a three-week siege at Pleiku, Hue was withdrawn on 18 April and Da Nang was held. With no double collapse in March, the Politburo put Saigon back to the dry season of 1976. The end state moves for the first time, from rung (a) to (b): a reprieve of about a year, with the Republic's fall expected between February and May 1976.

## Memo 012 — Combined US–RVN–ROK–Australian operations command; combined interagency task force against the VCI

Memorandum 012 gave the war a combined command and a finishing arm against the infrastructure, and the second mattered more. The combined command survived Khanh's coup by passing its orders through his office (EV012-1). It closed seams the enemy then stopped using, and made Hue one battle that ended five days early (EV000-44). Its transfer to Vietnamese command began in the Delta in 1966 and stopped at the palace's corps commanders (EV012-6), and an agent sat in its plans cell for two and a half years (EV012-7). The task force broke the Can Giuoc security section in 1964 and, in FOLLOW THROUGH, the Saigon–Gia Dinh Region's tax administration west of Saigon (EV012-2, EV012-4). At Tet the attackers crossed Hoc Mon with no one to guide them (EV012-8). On the coast its list killed a family and was abandoned (EV012-5). The end state does not move: rung (b), with the Republic's fall expected in 1976.

## Memo 013 — The air campaign against the North unrestricted: an opening strike on the full target list on 2 March 1965, and MACV targeting authority with standing restrike, no Hanoi or Haiphong zones, one strike on Haiphong's port, a 15-mile Chinese buffer and no pauses

Memorandum 013 gave the theater the air campaign it asked for throughout the war, in 1965. The President approved an opening strike on the whole target list and a campaign run from Saigon without zones around Hanoi or Haiphong and without pauses. On 2–9 March 1965 the B-52Js destroyed the North's power, fuel, great bridges, jet base and Haiphong's cranes in a week, and the air war was fought from ahead for three years: about 810–880 aircraft were lost rather than 922. The North dispersed, Moscow and Beijing rebuilt its sky, and the flow south never noticed. In October 1966 this command reported that the campaign destroyed everything that could be destroyed and that the South's war needed none of it. With no partial halt to trade in March 1968, the Paris talks opened in November rather than May, at no cost to the settlement. The end state is unchanged: the record's most direct test of whether anything reaches Hanoi's will found that nothing does.

## CP03 — Checkpoint

Checkpoint CP03 reviewed memoranda 011–013, consolidated Phase III, and answered three questions the user asked about them. The unrestricted opening strike of 1965 took the North's economy in a week and did not reach the South, whose needs were small and carried through Laos; the trucks Moscow sent instead of factories went to the Trail. The campaign against the infrastructure, now judged in units after revision R03 retired the abstract scale, held about a tenth more of III and IV Corps' rural people after dark than history's by 1967, six months to a year ahead of history's pacification, and never reached I and II Corps, where the war was lost. Its files held the political half of Tet and not its date, so the surprise stayed national. The end state stays at rung (b).
